event: Frederic Allen Williams is born, son of Dr. Frederic Allen and Elizabeth Paine Williams.
Williams keeps a studio in New York from this year (later at 58 West 57th Street).
Williams photographed in Taos modeling "The Sioux Worshipper" sundial.
Slides of Taos women photographed in Bert Phillips's studio and patio; Williams's Maid of Taos and related sculptures draw on these sittings.
source: HRC-5154 slide label; Jesse Ritner introduction

event: Studio portraits: Williams sits on Chief Blanket 2148-606 beside the composite sampler 2148-588 and The Arrowmaker.
Williams lectures on the "Arts of the Americas" with Kodachrome lantern slides (tenth year of lectures by the time of the brochure).

UT Board of Regents accepts a Deed of Trust conveying Williams's entire collection: sculpture, Indian textiles, baskets, pottery and artifacts, the Horse Museum, and books, photographs and lantern slides. Williams keeps possession during his lifetime.
confidence: documented (date not yet read from the document)

event: Collection held in storage at the Balcones Research Center, where it is catalogued.
Texas Memorial Museum catalog cards made for the textiles.

Texas Memorial Museum accessions the collection as Acc. No. 2148 ('Received from: Storage at Balcones, Williams Collection'), accessioned by Mary Carnahan. Other items from the collection are under TMM Acc. No. 1654.

Textiles held by the Department of Art and Art History, photographed for the DASe Visual Resources Collection by Steve Bourget and Kimberly L. Jones; some shown on rotating display at the Blanton Museum of Art.
Williams's photographs and lantern slides held by the Harry Ransom Center (Frederic Allen Williams Photograph Collection and Lantern Slide Collection).
Alina Scott publishes Woven into History; Jesse Ritner publishes Frederic Allen Williams: A Citizen Artist with a Magic Lantern.
The two archives are rejoined in this repository.
